_comment: U0a (docs/plans/simple-turn-pipeline-2026-09-22.md, point 4 and unit U0a). The owner's own failed turns today, verbatim, plus controls. Loaded by scripts/bench/replay.ts and run through the same fixture-conversation runner conversation.ts's --live mode uses (conversationRunner.ts, conversationScore.ts), three repeats each. Every row's `expect` follows conversationFixture.ts's TurnExpectation shape (JSON-compatible subset only): toolRan, outcomeArgsMatch (websearch's own argument key is `expression`, not `query` - conversationFixture.ts's existing websearch rows confirm this), sourcesNonEmpty, mustContain, mustNotContain. replay.ts adds the universal 'no stuck line, no honesty line' mustNotContain to every turn automatically, so it is not repeated below. No household member is named in any row (the org PII rule and the plan's point 4: 'none of which names a household member').

The seeded row is a remembered lookup that came back empty, the exact shape that leaked.

seedRecords.text: Searched for when the president of Chile was born; the search found nothing.

turns.say: this is the new reply engine

failed.note: OPENER-01/COMMAND-FAIL-01 (dev.md 'The knowledge hijack'): knowledge's own 'what is *' bound the whole question to `topic` and ran it as a Wikipedia page title; the lookup failed with a 502 and the raw MCP error string, carrying a Wikipedia URL, reached Jesse verbatim. commandsNode now refuses a question-word wildcard opener on anything but a directive turn (OPENER-01) - the manifest still lists the pattern (removing it broke the old, frozen path's own routing-corpus fixture, found live building this item; flagged for the coordinator, not fixed here), but the runtime gate never fires it on this question - and a failed pattern outcome now continues the turn to the model instead of answering with the error text (COMMAND-FAIL-01). No via: pattern outcome on this turn either way, a reply from source: model (a search may run under the interim rule; toolRan is not asserted), judged by WRITTEN-PARITY-01's own bare-parity column.
